title: British-Indian Doctor's Gut-Friendly Pistachio Chocolate Frozen Yoghurt Recipe
excerpt: Dr Rupy Aujla shares a no-churn frozen dessert that combines live-culture yoghurt, pistachios, and dark chocolate for a treat that supports gut health without an ice cream maker.
body:
• British-Indian doctor and bestselling cookbook author Dr Rupy Aujla has shared a gut-friendly pistachio and chocolate frozen yoghurt recipe that requires no ice cream maker and uses probiotic-rich Greek yoghurt as its base.
  • The recipe combines pistachios, dark chocolate, and live-culture yoghurt — ingredients that support gut health through probiotics, fibre, and polyphenols.
  • Dr Aujla, who holds a Master's in Nutritional Medicine, is known for recipes designed to support gut, brain, and heart health with at least three portions of plants per serving.
  • The frozen dessert offers a healthier alternative to commercial ice cream while drawing on flavors familiar to Indian cuisine, where pistachios and cardamom-spiced yoghurt have long been staples.

A Doctor's Approach to Dessert

Dr Rupy Aujla, the British-Indian GP behind the bestselling Doctor's Kitchen cookbooks, has shared a recipe for gut-friendly pistachio and chocolate frozen yoghurt — a no-fuss dessert that delivers probiotics and fibre without the added sugars and stabilizers found in commercial ice cream.

The recipe, shared via Hindustan Times, uses thick Greek yoghurt as its base, blended with crushed pistachios and swirled with melted dark chocolate. The result is a frozen treat that looks indulgent but is built on ingredients Dr Aujla considers medicinal: live-culture yoghurt for gut microbiome support, pistachios for plant protein and fibre, and dark chocolate (or raw cacao) for polyphenols — the antioxidant compounds linked to reduced inflammation.

The Recipe

The frozen yoghurt comes together with minimal effort and no specialized equipment. Here is the method based on Dr Aujla's approach:

Ingredients:

  • 500g thick Greek yoghurt (full-fat, with live cultures)
  • 100g shelled pistachios, roughly chopped
  • 80g dark chocolate (70% cacao or higher), melted
  • 2 tablespoons raw honey or maple syrup
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • A pinch of cardamom powder (optional)

Method:

  1. In a large bowl, combine the Greek yoghurt with honey (or maple syrup), vanilla extract, and cardamom if using. Stir until smooth.
  2. Fold in roughly two-thirds of the chopped pistachios.
  3. Pour the mixture into a lined loaf tin or shallow baking tray and smooth the surface.
  4. Drizzle the melted dark chocolate over the top and use a knife or skewer to create swirls through the yoghurt.
  5. Scatter the remaining pistachios over the surface and press gently.
  6. Freeze for at least four hours or overnight until firm.
  7. Remove from freezer five to ten minutes before serving. Slice or break into pieces.

"You can have indulgence and it can be healthy too. I want food and healthy food to be part of celebrations — something you share with the whole family."

— Dr Rupy Aujla, The Doctor's Kitchen

Why It Works for Gut Health

The recipe's gut-health credentials rest on its core ingredients. Greek yoghurt made with live bacterial cultures provides probiotics — beneficial bacteria that support digestion and immune function. Full-fat versions are preferred because the fat helps the probiotic organisms survive the journey through the digestive system.

Pistachios contribute prebiotic fibre, which feeds beneficial gut bacteria. Studies have shown that pistachio consumption can increase populations of butyrate-producing bacteria in the gut — microbes associated with reduced inflammation and improved intestinal barrier function. At roughly five grams of fibre per 100-gram serving, pistachios are among the most fibre-rich nuts available.

Dark chocolate, particularly varieties with 70% or higher cacao content, contains polyphenols that act as prebiotics in the lower gut. Research published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition has demonstrated that cocoa polyphenols can increase levels of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium, two genera commonly found in probiotic supplements.

Familiar Flavors, Healthier Format

For Indian diaspora cooks, the combination of pistachios and yoghurt is nothing new — pista kulfi, shrikhand, and pistachio-topped lassi are fixtures of Indian dessert culture. Dr Aujla, who is of Punjabi heritage, has built his career on bridging South Asian food traditions with evidence-based nutrition. His recipes frequently draw on Indian spice profiles — turmeric, ginger, cardamom — while grounding the approach in clinical research.

The frozen yoghurt stores well in the freezer for up to two weeks and can be adapted with seasonal additions: mango pulp in summer, pomegranate seeds in autumn, or a swirl of saffron-infused milk for a more traditional Indian flavour profile.
